lead: A JSP is an HTML page with Java inside. The container translates it into a servlet on first request, compiles it once, then reuses that servlet. You write the page, not println lines. JSF declares inputs and buttons as components, binds them to Java beans, and writes and reads HTML for you. Only a few universities still teach JSP and JSF; most new work uses Spring or React.
prereq: You need 4.7 for the servlet life cycle and HTML forms.

sections.h3: From hello.jsp to a running servlet

blocks.text: hello.jsp is plain text. On first request the container translates it to hello_jsp.java, which extends a JSP base servlet, compiles it to hello_jsp.class, loads it, and creates one instance.
This is the life cycle of 4.7 with two renamed methods.

Directives configure the page. <%@ page import="java.util.*" %> sets imports, content type or session use. <%@ include file="header.jsp" %> copies a file at translation time; <jsp:include page="..." /> runs at request time. <%@ taglib %> declares a tag library.

sections.h3: Scriptlets, implicit objects, EL and JSTL

blocks.text: Three tags carry Java: scriptlet <% %>, expression <%= %>, declaration <%! %>.
Nine implicit objects exist. Main five: request, response, out, session (see 4.6), application; rest are config, page, pageContext, exception.
EL reads values: ${param.name} is a parameter, ${sessionScope.user} a session attribute. JSTL: <c:forEach> loops, <c:if test="..."> decides, <c:out value="..." /> prints with HTML escaping.

sections.h3: MVC and the JSF component tree

blocks.text: A JSP should only display. A servlet controller reads parameters, calls model classes, stores results as request attributes, then forwards with request.getRequestDispatcher("/show.jsp").forward(request, response). The JSP prints ${student.marks}.

JSF builds on servlets. A Facelet (.xhtml) uses h: tags and the framework builds a component tree, one object per input/button. <h:inputText value="#{marksBean.name}"/> calls getName() when rendering and setName() on submit.

A JSF request has six phases: restore view, apply request values, process validations, update model values, invoke application, render response. required="true" is checked in phase three; on failure phases four and five are skipped, so your action never runs and the page redraws with the message.

spec.aria: Two columns: JSP goes from the query string to the param map to the EL line to the output; JSF goes from the form to the bean setters to the result page to the same output, Anu scored 78.

examples.question: A page must show Anu scored 78 from URL ?name=Anu&marks=78. Write the JSP with EL, then the JSF page and bean binding that show the same text.
steps: JSP path: the browser sends name=Anu and marks=78; the request parameter map holds both pairs.
show.jsp prints <p>${param.name} scored ${param.marks}</p> as Anu scored 78.
JSF path: marks.xhtml holds the form in the code block. The user types Anu and 78 and presses Show; a first GET does not copy query parameters into input components.
On postback JSF converts the values and calls setName("Anu") and setMarks(78) in apply request values / update model values.
The button returns result; navigation opens result.xhtml with #{marksBean.name} scored #{marksBean.marks}.
examples.answer: Both print Anu scored 78. The JSP reads the query string directly; JSF copies typed values into the bean after postback.
examples.check:
query = "name=Anu&marks=78"
params = dict(pair.split("=") for pair in query.split("&"))
print(int(params["marks"]))

code.code:
show.jsp:

${param.name} scored ${param.marks}

marks.xhtml: MarksBean: String name; int marks; getName/setName/getMarks/setMarks.

traps: JSP is not JavaScript: scriptlets run on the server; the browser receives only HTML.
EL does not escape HTML: ${param.name} is raw; use <c:out value="${param.name}" /> against script injection.
<%@ include %> merges at translation time; <jsp:include> runs at request time.
Failed JSF validation skips update model values and invoke application; setter and action do not run.
In JSF the container creates the bean; new MarksBean() gives a different object.

quiz.q: Name the three JSP scripting elements and the symbol of each.
Why is hello.jsp compiled once but _jspService run for every request?
quiz.a: Translation and compilation build the class once; that class is a servlet, so one instance serves every request.

quiz.q: A request carries ?city=Chennai&temp=34. Write the EL that prints Chennai is 34 C.
A student writes <% int hits = 0; hits++; %><%= hits %> and expects a counter shared by all users. Explain the result and the fix.
quiz.a: hits is a local variable of _jspService, recreated as 0 on each request, so the page always shows 1. Use an application attribute with synchronization or an AtomicInteger; a declaration <%! int hits = 0; %> is shared but hits++ is not thread-safe.

quiz.q: Write the Facelet that binds a text field to property amount of billBean and submits to outcome total.
What is the JSF component tree and when is it used?
quiz.a: A server-side tree of component objects, one per tag on the Facelet; it is restored at the start of a request and rendered at the end.

beyond: Not for the exam. JSP is in maintenance mode: new Java services usually return JSON from Spring Boot and let a React or Angular front end draw the page. JSF survives in long-lived enterprise portals and is specified as Jakarta Faces. Search 'Jakarta Server Pages specification', 'Facelets templating' and 'JSF life cycle phases' to go deeper.
